title: PAH-OMC-014 conditional convex separator for a component mismatch
question: If a future source-owned full-Q packet supplies one common positive lower bound for every component mismatch of one fixed common cylinder, what exact finite consequence follows for every normalized nonnegative sector mixture?
finding: Lean R504 proves that for a finite component index type, normalized nonnegative weights, and a common c>0 with c<=d(i) for every component mismatch d(i), the weighted mismatch sum_i w_i*d(i) is at least c and therefore nonzero. The integrated fixture gives weights (1/2,1/2), mismatches (1,3/2), c=1 and value 5/4; the independent fixture gives weights (1/3,1/3,1/3), mismatches (1,2,3), c=1 and value 2. No PAH component mismatch vector, sector law, projective kernel or separator is supplied.
decision_reason: R500-R503 separated projective recursion, nonzero-sector weight, and finite mixture error obligations. R504 adds the next conditional bridge: a source owner cannot obtain exact projective equality for a fixed cylinder from a mixture if all declared components share a source-proved positive mismatch. The theorem is deliberately agnostic about whether such a separator exists and does not turn the route-local Q=0 obstruction into a global no-go.
boundary: Conditional finite convex-separation support only. PAH-001 functional/rates, PAH-OMC-010 Gibbs weighting, PAH-OMC-012 full-Q graded domain/projection and PAH-OMC-014 order remain unchanged. R-484 hidden-diagonal defect 16/9 is retained and R-490 C_sw=540 remains domination-only. No source law, common embedding, tail estimate, projective equality, weak cylinder limit, positivity/normalization, stationarity, closability, semigroup, continuum or physical conclusion is claimed.
next_action: Obtain a source-owned exact mismatch vector for one fixed common cylinder over a declared finite component block and either a common positive separator or a convex-hull certificate that excludes zero, while separately supplying the normalized full-Q kernel/weight law and its tail control.
method: Hash-pin PAH-001, PAH-OMC-014, the projective-kernel obligation and the route-local Q=0 run.
Use the abstract finite weightedMismatch definition with no PAH-specific weights or mismatch values in the theorem.
Compile R504 under Lean 4.32.1 and verify its registry hash and no-escape-token policy.
Replay separate exact rational fixtures through integrated, independent and hostile mutation verifiers.
Keep the parent gate at HOLD_FOR_EVIDENCE because the source-owned mismatch vector, separator, full-Q law and tail estimate are absent.
assumptions: The future component index block is finite and common to the compared levels.
The future source-owned component mismatches d(i) are real values for one fixed bounded common cylinder.
The future weights are normalized and nonnegative.
The positive separator c is proved by the source owner rather than fitted after observing the cylinder.
The fixed PAH-001 functional, finite order and boundary conventions remain unchanged.
missing_assumptions: An exact source-owned mismatch vector for all components in a declared finite block.
A source-owned common positive separator or a convex-hull no-zero certificate.
A normalized full-Q Gibbs weight law or projective kernel and a common embedding/tail estimate.
A topology/Cauchy bound and a common stationarity domain for any later weak-limit argument.

adversarial_review.check: Does R504 choose or fit sector weights?
adversarial_review.disposition: UPHELD AS FALSE: weights are theorem variables only; no source-owned law is instantiated.

adversarial_review.check: Does the abstract separator prove that every PAH component has the same sign?
adversarial_review.disposition: UPHELD AS FALSE: the common positive lower bound is an uninstantiated future assumption.

adversarial_review.check: Does the finite theorem absorb a growing-Q tail or prove a projective limit?
adversarial_review.disposition: UPHELD AS FALSE: the finite block is explicit and tail, embedding and topology remain missing.

adversarial_review.check: Does the Q=0 route-local negative become a global full-Q no-go?
adversarial_review.disposition: UPHELD AS FALSE: Q=0 is retained only as a scoped obstruction and other components may cancel it.

adversarial_review.check: Are R-484 or C_sw=540 used to manufacture the separator?
adversarial_review.disposition: UPHELD AS FALSE: 16/9 remains a boundary defect and C_sw=540 is domination-only.

adversarial_review.check: Does this support a physical Pre-A, spacetime, QFT, gravity, Yang--Mills, mass-gap or TOE claim?
adversarial_review.disposition: UPHELD AS FALSE: all such interpretations remain explicit non-claims.

non_claims: No source-owned component mismatch vector or positive separator is supplied.
No full-Q Gibbs law, projective kernel, common embedding, tail bound or weak cylinder limit is proved.
No global projective no-go, R-488 nonzero, stationarity, closability or semigroup conclusion follows.
No physical Pre-A, spacetime, QFT, gravity, Yang--Mills, mass-gap or TOE conclusion follows.
Markov time remains external stochastic time.
revisit_condition: Reopen when a source owner supplies the exact all-component mismatch vector plus a common positive separator or convex-hull no-zero certificate, and independently supplies the normalized full-Q kernel/weight and tail data; or when an exact parent-scope counterexample invalidates the R504 finite theorem.
